name: GitHub
summary: GitHub doesn't review OAuth apps. You can register one and have any user connect within 15 minutes. The real decisions are OAuth App vs GitHub App, and planning for organizations that must approve your app before it can see their private repos.

verdict.label: Instant
verdict.approvalWait: None from GitHub. Each organization that restricts OAuth apps must approve yours.
verdict.handsOnEffort: Under an hour, including the callback code

decideFirst.question: OAuth App or GitHub App?
decideFirst.guidance: GitHub recommends GitHub Apps. They use fine-grained permissions, let users pick which repos the app can access, and use short-lived tokens. They can also act without a user. OAuth Apps act only as the user, use broad scopes, and are simpler. For an agent that touches user repos, prefer a GitHub App.

decideFirst.question: Personal account or organization owner?
decideFirst.guidance: Register the app under an organization you administer so users see your company, not a person, and so the app survives staff changes. A user or org can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

phases.name: 1 · Register the app
phases.goal: Get a client ID and secret

steps.title: Open Developer settings
steps.detail: Go to Profile → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth apps → New OAuth App. For an org, use the org's Settings → Developer settings.

steps.title: Fill in name, homepage URL, description, and callback URL
steps.detail: Only use public information. Don't put internal URLs here. An OAuth App gets exactly one callback URL; a GitHub App can have several.

evidence.note: Some translated pages in GitHub's docs state the opposite. The English page is authoritative.

steps.title: Enable Device Flow if your agent runs in a CLI or headless context
Generate a client secret and store it
steps.detail: Store it in your secret manager and never commit it.

phases.name: 2 · Build and test the flow
phases.goal: A user can connect and you get a token

steps.title: Implement authorize → callback → token exchange
steps.detail: Send users to /login/oauth/authorize with a random state value, then exchange the code at /login/oauth/access_token. Codes expire after 10 minutes. The agent can write and test this code.

steps.title: Test with a second GitHub account
steps.detail: Make sure scopes and the consent page look right to a user who isn't you.

evidence.note: Recommended practice, not a documented requirement

phases.name: 3 · Roll out to organizations
phases.goal: Your app can see org resources

steps.title: Expect org owner approval
steps.detail: New organizations have OAuth app access restrictions on by default. Members must ask an org owner to approve your app. Until then the app sees only public org resources. Tell users this in your UI.

requirements.item: Homepage URL and one callback URL
Users must have a verified email address

requirements.note: A GitHub Marketplace listing is separate and optional. Not covered here.

blockers.cause: The redirect_uri's host and port must exactly match the callback URL, and its path must be the same as or below the callback path
blockers.fix: Use the registered callback, or a subpath of it. For loopback callbacks such as http://127.0.0.1/path, the port can differ.

evidence.note: Confirmed in several versions of GitHub's docs

blockers.symptom: Connected user can't see org private repos
blockers.cause: The org has OAuth app access restrictions and hasn't approved your app
blockers.fix: The user requests approval and an org owner grants it under Org Settings → Third-party access → OAuth app policy.

blockers.cause: GitHub keeps at most 10 tokens per user/app/scope combination and revokes the oldest
blockers.fix: Reuse stored tokens instead of re-running the flow each session.

nuances.title: Token lifetimes differ by app type
nuances.detail: OAuth App tokens don't expire by default. GitHub App user tokens expire after 8 hours, with refresh tokens that last 6 months. This is on by default for new GitHub Apps. Your agent must handle refresh.

nuances.title: Using a refresh token invalidates the old pair
nuances.detail: Each refresh returns a new access and refresh token. Store them together, and handle concurrent refreshes carefully.

Default-on org access restrictions and the approval path against GitHub org docs

corrected: Some Japanese-language versions of the 'Creating an OAuth app' page say the reverse about which app type supports multiple callback URLs. The current English page says OAuth Apps get one and GitHub Apps can have several. We follow the English page.
unverified: The redirect-URI matching rules come from Enterprise Server versions of the docs seen in search results. They are consistent across versions but were not re-read on the current github.com page.
We did not register a live app in this run. That needs a signed-in GitHub account.
